content:
I just opened cslib#854 : The PR shows that all functions between finite types are multi-tape-TM-computable in constant time and space. The result is "obvious" but my hope was that it captures many useful functions.

It opens up two new areas for TMs:

1) it defines the concept of encoding - I think we need that to make talking about functions convenient. The PR itself leaves the definition of encoding very vague to begin with, it does not even require a computable decoding function. I think this is good for now (especially for finite types) - in the end you always have to specify an explicit encoding anyway - and we can change it later

2) it's the first file in a larger collection of combinators. I imagine it to contain a collection of results of the form "if the functions list, step and init have this and that complexity, then fun x => (list x).foldl step (init x) has that complexity". I prototyped such a library in my personal fork using AI and it seems to work well.
